## 3. Runtime and constraints

Compiled by `pyc.py` for `py_core`; only this subset is allowed (anything else is rejected at compile time):

```text
ints, True/False/None, names, + - & | ^ << >> ~ unary -, not/and/or
  in conditions, one comparison per expression (< <= > >= == !=),
  mem32[addr] loads/stores (also mem32[a] op= v), name op= expr,
  if/elif/else, while/break/continue, pass, global, import (ignored).
  "from <name> import *" where <name>.py sits next to the source file
  inlines that file there (once), so firmware can be split into modules
  that share one global namespace; errors name the original file / line.
  Without such a file, "from <name> import *" reads the SystemVerilog
  package <name>.sv found next to the source or in a -I directory (the
  memory map packages, e.g. video_processor_map_pkg.sv): its
  "localparam ... NAME = expr;" lines become UPPER_CASE constants NAME
  (folded), "import <pkg>::*;" loads that package first, <pkg>::NAME and
  SV literals (32'h0001_0000, 'h40, 16'd10) are understood, so the
  firmware takes its addresses from the same file as the RTL decoders.
  UPPER_CASE module-level names bound once to a constant expression
  (or const(expr)) are folded at compile time.
  def f(a, b): ... return x   functions with positional parameters,
  called as f(x, y) in expressions or statements; recursion is allowed
  up to the core's call depth. Missing return -> None.
  A function passed to irq_handler() is an interrupt handler instead:
  no parameters, no return value, cannot be called directly.
Builtins: irq_handler(fn), irq_enable(), irq_disable(), wait_irq(), halt(value).
  wait_irq() (WAIT_IRQ, 0x3E) stops the core until its interrupt input is high (an enabled
  source pending at the intc), whether interrupts are enabled or not; with them disabled the
  code after it runs first (the race-free sleep: disable, test, wait_irq, enable).
Strings: a string literal (in any expression, e.g. puts("text")) is a
  small int handle; the text goes to a string table in flash at
  STR_BASE (0x8000), outside the boot image, for the firmware to read at
  run time through the flash controller. The table has 512 slots of 64
  bytes (0x8000-0xFFFF): [0] length (0..62), [1] 1 if the string
  continues in the next slot, [2..] the bytes. A handle is the first slot
  number; slots 128..255 are emitted as h - 256 so they fit LOAD_SMALL,
  slots 256..511 as h (a constant). Firmware decodes a handle with
  slot = h if h >= 256 else h & 255.
  strings("a", "b", ...) returns the handle of a block of consecutive
  one-slot strings (each <= 62 bytes), so handle + i selects entry i (a
  block never straddles slot 256, so the decoding holds for handle + i).
  Identical strings share slots.
Not in the hardware fast path (rejected): * / % ** on variables (py_core v1),
** always, default/keyword arguments, closures, lists, dicts, floats, classes.
--core 2 (py_core v2): * // % on variables (BINARY_MUL 0x17, BINARY_FLOORDIV
  0x1E, BINARY_MOD 0x1F: Python's floor division and modulo, a zero
  divisor traps), 256 globals and 32 locals per function.
```

- Register addresses come from the SystemVerilog map packages (`from <pkg> import *`), never hard-coded numbers, so firmware and RTL decoders share one source.
- Every hardware wait has a bound (poll count) and reports a timeout instead of hanging.

- Every register access must match the register map of the block it addresses (its `<ip>/docs/<ip>_prompt.md` section 5/6 and `src/include/<ip>_regs.json`): offset, access type (RO / RW / W1C / CMD), bit fields and reset values.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference program's documentation):

```text
video_processor firmware: object detection and tracking (section 8).

The camera may send several tracking sequences one after the other (camera register 0x56, the
count; 0x57 the number of the sequence whose settings are loaded): for each, the sequence's frame
size comes from the camera (registers 0x30-0x33) and is set in every block; so are the object
classes to detect, their symbol styles and the most targets tracked at a time (registers 0x50-0x55
and 0x58, camera_detect) and the image name (0x40-0x4F). Each selected class's detector searches the whole
frame and symbol_overlay waits for a target. The transcript logs the first stage, the tracker and
the last stage of every frame (only the tracker with the direct-transcript strap); on each tracker
event (track_event) the firmware reads every selected detector's blobs, checks their shapes
(class_ok), matches them to the class's tracks (tracker.py), moves each target's box (overlay.py) to
its predicted position for the next frame, and completes the event's line with the results: per
target its class letter, its label (P<n> person, G<n> ground transport, A<n> aircraft: drawn below
its symbol; - a face of a labelled pedestrian), state, measured box and pixels, and the box the
overlay draws on the next frame.
```

Per function:

```text
track_setup: Sequence seq_no of total: every block for the camera's frame size; the selected detectors searching, overlay on, no
box yet.

detector_select: The NPU detector and ByteTrack when the NPU and its program are there (the feature detectors then
stay off), else the feature detectors and their tracker (npu_mode 0).

feature_setup: feature_detect for the sequence: the frame size, edges (Sobel above 128, filled over 8 pixels),
motion (20 beyond the background cell's range, filled over 2, background rate 1/4), the camera shift
found automatically; restarted, so its first frame fills the background.

class_letter: Class tag of the transcript: P pedestrian, F face, A automobile, V vehicle, J aircraft (jet).

track_report: Target k of class c after its step (r: track_step's result, i: its blob or -1, first: its
class's first target on the line): its part of the line and its box for the next frame;
returns 1 when the target is still tracked.

next_box: Target k of class c (SCRATCH word b of detector t): its box at the predicted position for the
next frame, printed as the overlay draws it.

new_blob: Blob i of detector t can start a target of class c: its shape, and not the same object as a
target of the class already (another term's blob of it).

biggest_blob: The unused blob of detector t with the most pixels that can start a target of class c, or -1.

face_of: A confirmed face target inside the box of the pedestrian at SCRATCH word b of detector t (or
just above it: the head over a dark body): its number, or -1.

free_track: A free track of detector t's class, or -1.

track_class: Class c's step on this frame's blobs: every live target takes its nearest blob (or coasts),
blobs left over start new targets; prints the class's part of the transcript line (part: not
the first class on it). Returns 1 when the class has a target tracked.

track_event: Tracker event of frame n (events.py): every selected class measured, stepped, its boxes
moved; completes the transcript line ("tracker frame n:" then, per class, its targets). trk_frames
counts the event once the boxes are committed (the testbench sends the next GIF frame after
that).

track_sequence: One tracking sequence: set up, then the transcript with one tracking step per tracker event
until the camera's sequence (GPIO0[29] = 1) has ended and the pipeline is empty.

track: Section 8: every tracking sequence the camera sends (register 0x56), each once the camera has
loaded its settings (register 0x57 = its number).
```

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the program.

```text
// Industry reference check - tracking.py (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] P. R. Kalata, "The Tracking Index: A Generalized Parameter for alpha-beta and alpha-
//   beta-gamma Target Trackers", IEEE Trans. AES 20(2):174-182, 1984; summary
//   https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_beta_filter (x_p = x + v T; r = z - x_p; x += alpha r;
//   v += beta r / T)
//   [2] I. Haritaoglu, D. Harwood, L. S. Davis, "W4: Real-time surveillance of people and their
//   activities", IEEE PAMI 22(8), 2000, doi:10.1109/34.868683 (background as per-pixel minimum
//   / maximum intensity, foreground outside it)
//   [3] K. Ratakonda, "Real-time digital video stabilization for multi-media applications",
//   ISCAS 1998 vol. 4 pp. 69-72 (row / column integral projections, 1-D shift search by minimum
//   SAD)
//   [4] Register maps of the addressed blocks: <ip>/src/include/<ip>_regs.json and section 5/6
//   of <ip>/docs/<ip>_prompt.md (video_pipeline, vision_system, blur_sharpen, frame_counter,
//   object_tracker, feature_detect, symbol_overlay, py_soc peripherals)
// Published algorithm / rules:
//   Firmware rules: the pyc.py subset; register offsets, access types and bit fields as in the
//   blocks' register maps. Detector / feature set-up per object_tracker and feature_detect.
// Comparison with this program (section 6):
//   Matches: per-class detector set-up, feature_detect motion / edge settings, sequence
//   handling.
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```
